title: Each oriented Reidemeister move is realized by an ambient isotopy
statement: Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of oriented links $L,L'$. If $D'$ is obtained from $D$ by one oriented Reidemeister move (or by a planar isotopy), then $L$ and $L'$ are equivalent oriented links. More precisely the move is realized by an ambient isotopy of $S^3$ supported in a small ball meeting the projection plane in the disk of the move.
strategy: Local models, one per move: R1 pulls a kink straight or introduces it, inside a ball around the kink; R2 slides one of the two strands over or under the other; R3 passes the moving strand across the crossing of the other two. In each case the over/under data select the side of the plane on which the strands are placed, so the explicit isotopy is the obvious linear interpolation in the ball; a planar isotopy of diagrams is the projection of an ambient isotopy of the plane crossed with the identity. This is the easy direction of Reidemeister's theorem.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
